audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Galileans/tower warning, fig tree parable, Sabbath healing of bent woman, mustard/leaven, narrow door, and Jerusalem lament.

verses.restored: At that same time some were present reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

familiar.text: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

modern.text: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

original.text: Παρῆσαν δέ τινες ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ καιρῷ ἀπαγγέλλοντες αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν Γαλιλαίων ὧν τὸ αἷμα Πιλᾶτος ἔμιξεν μετὰ τῶν θυσιῶν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: He answered them, Do you think these Galileans became greater sinners/misaligned ones than all the Galileans because they suffered these things?

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?

modern.text: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this fate?

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Δοκεῖτε ὅτι οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι οὗτοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ πάντας τοὺς Γαλιλαίους ἐγένοντο, ὅτι ⸀ταῦτα πεπόνθασιν;

verses.restored: No, I say to you; but unless you turn/realign, you will all likewise perish.

familiar.text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

modern.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.

original.text: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἐὰν μὴ μετανοῆτε πάντες ⸀ὁμοίως ἀπολεῖσθε.

verses.restored: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them, do you think they became debtors beyond all the people dwelling in Jerusalem?

familiar.text: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

modern.text: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?

original.text: ἢ ἐκεῖνοι οἱ ⸀δεκαοκτὼ ἐφʼ οὓς ἔπεσεν ὁ πύργος ἐν τῷ Σιλωὰμ καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτούς, δοκεῖτε ὅτι ⸀αὐτοὶ ὀφειλέται ἐγένοντο παρὰ πάντας ⸀τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ⸀κατοικοῦντας Ἰερουσαλήμ;

verses.restored: No, I say to you; but unless you turn/realign, you will all likewise perish.

familiar.text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

modern.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.” The Parable of the Barren Fig Tree (Isaiah 5:1–7)

original.text: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἐὰν μὴ ⸀μετανοῆτε πάντες ⸀ὡσαύτως ἀπολεῖσθε.

verses.restored: He spoke this parable: A certain person had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.

familiar.text: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.

modern.text: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but did not find any.

original.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ ταύτην τὴν παραβολήν. Συκῆν εἶχέν τις ⸂πεφυτευμένην ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι αὐτοῦ⸃, καὶ ἦλθεν ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ οὐχ εὗρεν.

verses.restored: He said to the vineyard-worker, Look, three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and found none. Cut it down. Why should it make the ground useless?

familiar.text: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?

modern.text: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὸν ἀμπελουργόν· Ἰδοὺ τρία ἔτη ⸂ἀφʼ οὗ⸃ ἔρχομαι ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν τῇ συκῇ ταύτῃ καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκω· ⸀ἔκκοψον αὐτήν· ἱνατί καὶ τὴν γῆν καταργεῖ;

verses.restored: But he answered, Lord, leave it also this year, until I dig around it and put manure.

familiar.text: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:

modern.text: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἄφες αὐτὴν καὶ τοῦτο τὸ ἔτος, ἕως ὅτου σκάψω περὶ αὐτὴν καὶ βάλω κόπρια·

verses.restored: If it makes fruit in the future, good; but if not, you will cut it down.

familiar.text: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

modern.text: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’” Jesus Heals a Disabled Woman

original.text: κἂν μὲν ποιήσῃ καρπὸν ⸂εἰς τὸ μέλλον— εἰ δὲ μήγε,⸃ ἐκκόψεις αὐτήν.

verses.restored: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.

familiar.text: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

modern.text: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,

original.text: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν.

verses.restored: Look, a woman had a spirit of weakness eighteen years; she was bent over and not able to straighten herself completely.

familiar.text: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself.

modern.text: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ⸀γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη ⸀δεκαοκτώ, καὶ ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές.

verses.restored: Seeing her, Jesus called out and said to her, Woman, you have been released from your weakness.

familiar.text: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

modern.text: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”

original.text: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Γύναι, ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου,

verses.restored: He placed hands on her, and immediately she was made straight, and she glorified the Divine.

familiar.text: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

modern.text: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.

original.text: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας· καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη, καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεόν.

verses.restored: The synagogue ruler, indignant because Jesus healed on the Sabbath, answered the crowd, There are six days in which it is necessary to work; therefore come and be healed on them, and not on the Sabbath day.

familiar.text: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

modern.text: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ⸀ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι· ἐν ⸀αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου.

verses.restored: The Lord answered him, Hypocrites, does not each of you on the Sabbath loose his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away to water?

familiar.text: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?

modern.text: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν· Ὑποκριταί, ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ⸀ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει;

verses.restored: And this daughter of Abraham, whom the Adversary bound, look, eighteen years, was it not necessary to loose her from this bond on the Sabbath day?

familiar.text: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

modern.text: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”

original.text: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;

verses.restored: As he said these things, all those opposing him were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced over all the glorious things happening through him.

familiar.text: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

modern.text: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing. The Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32; Mark 4:30–34)

original.text: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντος αὐτοῦ κατῃσχύνοντο πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἔχαιρεν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He said, What is the reign of the Divine like, and to what shall I compare it?

familiar.text: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?

modern.text: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?

original.text: Ἔλεγεν ⸀οὖν· Τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν;

verses.restored: It is like a mustard seed that a person took and threw into his garden; it grew and became a tree, and the birds of heaven nested in its branches.

familiar.text: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.

modern.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.” The Parable of the Leaven (Matthew 13:33)

original.text: ὁμοία ἐστὶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔβαλεν εἰς κῆπον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ηὔξησεν καὶ ἐγένετο εἰς ⸀δένδρον, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Again he said, To what shall I compare the reign of the Divine?

familiar.text: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

modern.text: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?

original.text: ⸀Καὶ πάλιν εἶπεν· Τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ;

verses.restored: It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all was leavened.

familiar.text: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

modern.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.” The Narrow Door (Matthew 7:13–14)

original.text: ὁμοία ἐστὶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ⸀ἔκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.

verses.restored: He traveled through cities and villages, teaching and making his journey toward Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.

modern.text: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.

original.text: Καὶ διεπορεύετο κατὰ πόλεις καὶ κώμας διδάσκων καὶ πορείαν ποιούμενος εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα.

verses.restored: Someone said to him, Lord, are few being saved/healed? He said to them,

familiar.text: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,

modern.text: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?” Jesus answered,

original.text: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.restored: Strive to enter through the narrow door, because many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be strong enough.

familiar.text: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

modern.text: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.

original.text: Ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς ⸀θύρας, ὅτι πολλοί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν,

verses.restored: Once the house-master rises and shuts the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock, saying, Lord, open to us, he will answer, I do not know where you are from.

familiar.text: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

modern.text: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’

original.text: ἀφʼ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἄρξησθε ἔξω ἑστάναι καὶ κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες· ⸀Κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν· καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ.

verses.restored: Then you will begin to say, We ate and drank before you, and you taught in our streets.

familiar.text: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

modern.text: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’

original.text: τότε ἄρξεσθε λέγειν· Ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας·

verses.restored: He will say, I do not know where you are from; depart from me, all workers of injustice.

familiar.text: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

modern.text: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’

original.text: καὶ ἐρεῖ ⸀λέγων ὑμῖν· Οὐκ ⸀οἶδα πόθεν ἐστέ· ἀπόστητε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, πάντες ⸀ἐργάται ἀδικίας.

verses.restored: There will be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the reign of the Divine, but yourselves cast outside.

familiar.text: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

modern.text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.

original.text: ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων, ὅταν ⸀ὄψησθε Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ καὶ πάντας τοὺς προφήτας ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑμᾶς δὲ ἐκβαλλομένους ἔξω.

verses.restored: They will come from east and west, north and south, and recline in the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

modern.text: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.

original.text: καὶ ἥξουσιν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν καὶ ⸀ἀπὸ βορρᾶ καὶ νότου καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Look, some are last who will be first, and some are first who will be last.

familiar.text: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.

modern.text: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.” Lament over Jerusalem (Matthew 23:37–39)

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἰσὶν ἔσχατοι οἳ ἔσονται πρῶτοι, καὶ εἰσὶν πρῶτοι οἳ ἔσονται ἔσχατοι.

verses.restored: At that hour some Pharisees came and said to him, Go out and depart from here, because Herod wants to kill you.

familiar.text: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.

modern.text: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”

original.text: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ⸀ὥρᾳ προσῆλθάν τινες Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε καὶ πορεύου ἐντεῦθεν, ὅτι Ἡρῴδης θέλει σε ἀποκτεῖναι.

verses.restored: He said to them, Go tell that fox, Look, I cast out unclean spirits and complete healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am completed.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες εἴπατε τῇ ἀλώπεκι ταύτῃ· Ἰδοὺ ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια καὶ ἰάσεις ⸀ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ τελειοῦμαι.

verses.restored: Nevertheless, it is necessary for me to travel today, tomorrow, and the next day, because it is not fitting for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

modern.text: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.

original.text: πλὴν δεῖ με σήμερον καὶ αὔριον καὶ τῇ ἐχομένῃ πορεύεσθαι, ὅτι οὐκ ἐνδέχεται προφήτην ἀπολέσθαι ἔξω Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.restored: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one killing the prophets and stoning those sent to her. How often I wanted to gather your children as a hen gathers her brood under wings, and you were not willing.

familiar.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!

modern.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

original.text: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν— ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυνάξαι τὰ τέκνα σου ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις τὴν ἑαυτῆς νοσσιὰν ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε.

verses.restored: Look, your house is left to you. I say to you, you will certainly not see me until you say, Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord.

familiar.text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

modern.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”

original.text: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ⸀ὑμῶν. λέγω ⸀δὲ ⸀ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ⸂ἴδητέ με⸃ ἕως ⸂ἥξει ὅτε⸃ εἴπητε· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.
